extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and processing amendments to patent applications (claims, drawings, specification) and for use/evaluation of affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 to antedate references. Covers procedural requirements, restrictions (no new matter), treatment of noncompliant/amendments after final, and form-paragraph practice for examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — Amendment by rewriting; directions to cancel or add
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting such claim with all changes (e.g., additions, deletions, modifications) included. The rewriting of a claim (with the same number) will be construed as directing the cancellation of the previous version of that claim. A claim may also be canceled by an instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rewritten or newly added claim must be in clean form (without markings). A parenthetical expression should follow the claim number indicating status (e.g., "amended," "twice amended," or "new"). If amended by rewriting with the same number, the amendment must be accompanied by a marked-up version on separate paper showing all changes relative to the previous version (brackets for deletions, underlining for additions, or equivalent). The parenthetical status must be the same on both the clean and marked-up versions. A marked-up version is not required for an added claim or a canceled claim; it is sufficient to state that a claim has been added or canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canceled matter cannot be reinstated by amendment as the same claim number; it must be presented as a new insertion or a new claim number when reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated clean version of all pending claims (37 CFR 1.121(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A clean version of the entire set of pending claims may be submitted in a single amendment paper. Such a submission shall be construed as directing the cancellation of all previous versions of any pending claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up version is required only for claims being changed by the current amendment. Any claim not accompanied by a marked-up version will constitute an assertion that it has not been changed relative to the immediate prior version. When consolidating, parenthetical expressions identifying particular prior versions should not be rewritten; claims rewritten in clean form should retain the same claim numbers and be submitted in proper numerical order except for canceled claims. The examiner has no responsibility to ensure the accuracy of applicant's claim rewriting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — procedure for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the application drawings must be submitted on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon approval by the examiner, new drawings in compliance with § 1.84 including the changes must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be required to align specification language and drawings with claim scope; the Office may direct such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments must be supported by original disclosure; additions that introduce new, unsupported subject matter are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, of an application made by the Office in an examiner’s amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner’s amendment by identifying the precise point in the specification or the claim(s) where the insertion or deletion is to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with the normal claimant-amendment form requirements (e.g., paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), (c)(1)) is not required for examiner's amendments; the examiner can direct precise insertions/deletions as part of an examiner's amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reissue, reexamination, and provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications must be made in accordance with § 1.173. Proposed amendments to patents in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530(d)-(j). Amendments in provisional applications are not normally made; if made they must comply with the provisions of this section and will be placed in the provisional file but may not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different statutory/regulatory regimes apply to reissue, reexamination, and provisional filings — follow cited sections for specific procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'brackets'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'brackets' set forth in 37 CFR 1.121 means square brackets, thus: [ ]. It does not encompass and is to be distinguished from parentheses ().

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-compliant amendments (preliminary and non-final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments and non-final amendments which are not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 are handled by the technical support staff. The technical support staff notifies applicant of the defects by mailing a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff briefly review papers before entry to determine discourteous remarks or compliance defects. Non-compliant preliminary/non-final amendments invoke a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment from technical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments submitted after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted after a final rejection are to be forwarded in unentered status to the examiners, who should address any non-compliance issues in an advisory action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment after final fails to place the application in condition for allowance by removing all rejections/objections from the final rejection, the examiner notifies applicant in an advisory action. If the amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121 and is considered informal, the examiner should provide reasons and require resubmission within any remaining period of time set in the final rejection. No extensions of time or new time periods that would extend the six-month statutory period will be set in the advisory action. If time remains, applicants may re-submit the amendment or request an extension of time (with fee), but cannot obtain an extension beyond the six-month statutory deadline. Submission near the end of the statutory period should be accompanied by filing a Notice of Appeal to avoid abandonment risk prior to examiner action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' duty when directions for entry of an amendment are defective
rubrics_metrics.description: The directions for the entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph number, lack of precision). If the correct place of entry is clear from the context, the amendatory paper will be properly amended in the Technology Center and a notation thereof, initialed in ink by the examiner, will be made on the margin of the amendatory paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the next Office action the applicant should be informed of this alteration and the entry of the amendment as thus amended. The applicant should also be informed of nonentry where defective directions and context leave doubt as to intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of amendments (replacement paragraphs/sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph or section to the specification is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled, so that no interlineations or deletions shall appear in the clause as finally presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct with decorum and discourtesy handling (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the Patent and Trademark Office with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation will be submitted to the Commissioner and will be returned by direct order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff should briefly review papers before entry to detect discourteous remarks. If attorney/agent is discourteous in remarks or arguments in an amendment, either ignore the discourtesy or submit the paper to the Technology Center Director for potential return. Complaints against examiners/employees must be made in separate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration may be submitted when any claim of an application or a patent under reexamination is rejected, to establish invention of the subject matter of the rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference or activity on which the rejection is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date of references (U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or international application publication under PCT Article 21(2)) is the earlier of its publication date or date that it is effective as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). Prior invention under 1.131 may not be established in countries other than the United States, a NAFTA country, or a WTO member country, subject to specified effective dates for NAFTA and WTO recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required character and weight of the showing under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts shall be such, in character and weight, as to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference coupled with due diligence from prior to said date to a subsequent reduction to practice or to the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, must accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence satisfactorily explained. Conception must be capable of proof (demonstrative evidence or complete disclosure to another).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.131 may be used (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be used, for example: (A) To antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 102(b) (e.g., where the prior art date is less than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date). (B) To antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), where the reference has a 102(e) date prior to applicant's effective filing date and shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 715.05 for discussion of 'same patentable invention' and cited MPEP sections for what qualifies as 102(e) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.131 is inappropriate (A–J)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate in these situations: (A) reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)); (B) reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claims the same patentable invention; (C) reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant issued prior to the filing date of the domestic application on an application filed more than 12 months prior (35 U.S.C.102(d)); (D) effective filing date of applicant's parent or Convention priority predates the reference (making affidavit unnecessary); (E) reference is a prior U.S. patent to same entity claiming same invention (double patenting); (F) reference is disclosure of a prior U.S. patent to the same party, not copending (dedication); (G) applicant has clearly admitted on the record that subject matter relied on in the reference is prior art; (H) subject matter relied upon is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(f); (I) subject matter is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g); (J) subject matter corresponding to a lost count in an interference is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) or barred by interference estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.131 is designed to permit overcoming rejections based on references/activities which are not statutory bars but have dates prior to the effective filing date; when subject matter is available under 102(g) by definition it cannot be overcome by 1.131 because it must have been made before applicant's invention. See cited case law for nuances and exceptions (e.g., Zletz, Deckler, McKellin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference effective date to be overcome under 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to be overcome under 37 CFR 1.131 is the effective date of the reference (i.e., the date on which the reference is available as prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printed publication (including a published foreign patent application) is effective as of its publication date, not its date of receipt by the publisher. For U.S. patents/application publications, effective dates are governed by MPEP §§ 706.02(a), 2136–2136.03; where disclosure relied on was introduced by amendment as new matter, the date to be overcome is the date of amendment (see In re Willien).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities as prior art — effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity used to reject claims has an effective date equal to the date the activity was first known to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may make admissions or submit evidence of use/knowledge of the invention by others; examiner may have personal knowledge. See MPEP §§ 706.02(c), 2133.03 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.57–7.64 — examiner response templates for 1.131 affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs are provided for examiner use when responding to 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations: 7.57 (Ineffective — Heading), 7.58 (Ineffective — Claiming Same Invention), 7.59 (Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Reduction to Practice), 7.60 (Ineffective — Reference Is a Statutory Bar), 7.61 (Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Conception), 7.62 (Ineffective — Diligence Lacking), 7.63 (Ineffective — Insufficient Evidence of Actual Reduction to Practice), 7.64 (Effective To Overcome Reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph must be used with specified preceding/following paragraphs and examiner notes. Insert bracketed information and provide specific explanations in the indicated brackets (e.g., reasons for insufficiency, dates). Use appropriate sequencing when multiple deficiencies exist (e.g., follow 7.57 with 7.61 if conception insufficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 versus 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits — when to use each
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations are to overcome prior art rejections by proving invention of the claimed subject matter by applicant prior to the effective date of the reference. 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits/declarations are used to establish that the subject matter relied on in a patent or application publication was the invention of the applicant (i.e., to show a reference is applicant's own invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits submitted improperly under 1.131 but intended as 1.132 will be considered as though filed under 1.132. In some situations (e.g., 35 U.S.C.103 rejections relying on 102(f) or (g) references or on 102(e) references for applications filed on/after Nov 29, 1999) other proof (common ownership, derivation) may be necessary to overcome rejections — see MPEP § 706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint patent/application and co-authorship situations
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter is disclosed but not claimed in a patent or application publication filed jointly by applicant and another, the joint patent/application publication is a valid reference unless overcome by affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or an unequivocal declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 by applicant that he/she conceived or invented the subject matter relied on in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer by the other patentee/applicant should not be required but may be accepted. Where applicant is a co-author of a cited publication, applicant may overcome the rejection by filing an affidavit/declaration under 1.131 or a specific 1.132 establishing the article describes applicant's own work. Derivation must be shown by evidence that the patentee/applicant derived knowledge from applicant and that applicant made the invention on which the disclosure is based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common assignee references and effect on 1.131/1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that the reference patent or application publication and the application which claims the subject matter are owned by the same assignee does not avoid the necessity of filing an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131, in the absence of a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the patentee derived the subject matter from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common assignee does not by itself preclude rejections; however, a showing that the inventions were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time the later invention was made may preclude certain rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103/102(f)/(g) (see MPEP § 706.02(l)).
